_comment: pay_per_container_nm: a ship is paid capacity x leg distance (nm) x this rate when it finishes unloading; tuned so a Scooter 10 earns about $2,000 per minute of sailing. fuel_price: dollars per fuel unit, the same at every port (fuel is about 40% of a leg's pay). Breakdowns (from company level min_company_level): every interval_s seconds, each ship at sea (not recovery boats) rolls its own chance of losing hit of its maintenance (0.5 = 50 points). The chance runs from chance_at_full at 100% maintenance to chance_at_empty at 0%, times the model's breakdown_factor (bigger ships are sturdier), times an age factor (1 + age_per_hour_at_sea for each hour the ship has spent at sea, up to max_age_factor), less the durability skill. initial_view_width_deg: how many degrees of longitude the map shows across when it opens, centered on the home port.
_xp_comment: XP: every delivery (when unloading finishes) gives the company and the ship XP in proportion to its pay: pay / pay_per_container_nm x xp_per_container_nm (for container ships, containers x leg distance x xp_per_container_nm). Company levels run 1 to max_company_level. Level L costs (company_level_minutes[0] + company_level_minutes[1] x (L - 1)) minutes of the XP a full fleet at that level would earn at sea (at_sea_share of the time): every unlocked cargo model with all the slots it has at that level. So each level takes about as long no matter how big the fleet has become, and level 100 takes about 40 hours. ship_slots: how many of each model you can own. [start, every]: a model gets start slots when it unlocks and one more every that many company levels, up to its max_owned. cargo is container ships and gas tankers, recovery is recovery boats. Ships level 0 to ship_max_level, one skill point per level; see ship_models.json xp_first_level and ship_level_growth. skills: the bonus per skill level (speed: top speed +2%; durability: wear and breakdown chance -5%; efficiency: fuel burn -3%), up to skill_max_level each.
_hubs_comment: Headquarters and hubs: the HQ is at the home port from the start; one more hub every every_company_levels company levels, up to max_hubs, each placed for good at any port. A hub earns the XP of every delivery unloaded at its port and levels 0 to max_level; level L to L+1 costs (level_minutes[0] + level_minutes[1] x L) minutes of traffic_share of a full fleet's XP at the current company level, so a hub taking about a quarter of the fleet's deliveries maxes out in about 12.5 hours. Each level is an upgrade point for 4 paths of up to max_path_level points, and spending one costs upgrade_cost plus upgrade_cost_step for each point already in that path (1M, 1.25M, 1.5M...); per_point is each point's bonus to every ship docking there (xp: ship XP, costs: fuel and repair prices, speed: port stop time, pay: delivery pay). The HQ's bonuses are hq_multiplier times a hub's.
